name: Chin-Up
grip: Underhand supinated grip, shoulder-width apart, with palms facing toward the athlete.
description: Pull bodyweight vertically to an overhead bar using a shoulder-width supinated grip until the chin clears the bar, emphasizing the biceps brachii and lower latissimus fibers.
setup: Grasp an overhead bar with a shoulder-width supinated grip (palms facing inward toward your face).
Hang in a complete, active dead hang with arms fully extended and shoulders depressed away from ears.
Brace your core, cross your ankles slightly behind you, and keep a tall chest.
instructions: Pull your body upward by driving your elbows down and back toward your ribcage.
Lead with the upper chest and pull until your chin comfortably clears the top edge of the bar.
Pause briefly at peak contraction, squeezing your lats and biceps.
Lower your body in a slow, uniform descent back to a complete dead hang with arms fully extended before beginning the next repetition.
cues: Chest to the bar, chin clearly over.
Lower to a full dead hang on every rep.
commonMistakes: Kipping or swinging the hips and legs to generate upward momentum.
Cutting the bottom range of motion short without fully extending the elbows.
Reaching the chin upward frantically without completing full humeral adduction.

logging.example: Bodyweight: record repetitions performed (or note added external weight if dipping belt is used).
logging.note: Record clean repetitions performed from full hang to chin-over-bar.

variantNote: Supinated-grip vertical pull. Compared to the pronated pull-up, the underhand grip places the biceps brachii in an optimal line of pull for increased mechanical advantage and elbow flexion torque.
